In what year was Javier Milei born?
Javier Milei: Javier Gerardo Milei (born 22 October 1970) is an Argentine politician and economist who has served as the 57th president of Argentina since 2023.
In what year was HIV/AIDS discovered?
HIV/AIDS: The human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) is a retrovirus that attacks the immune system.
In what year was COVID-19 discovered?
COVID-19: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is a contagious disease caused by the coronavirus SARS-CoV-2.
Mannitol: Pfizer. Mannitol is a type of sugar alcohol used as a sweetener and medication.
Which country is Bombardier Global Express from?
Bombardier Global Express: Canada. The Bombardier Global Express is a large cabin, long-range business jet designed and manufactured by Bombardier Aviation.
Who is credited with discovering Special relativity?
Special relativity: Albert Einstein. In physics, the special theory of relativity, or simply special relativity, is a scientific theory of the relationship between space and time.
Who is credited with discovering Carbon dioxide?
Carbon dioxide: Jan Baptist van Helmont. Carbon dioxide is a chemical compound with the chemical formula CO2.
Who is credited with discovering Calcium?
Calcium: Humphry Davy. Calcium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ca and atomic number 20.
Sitting atop the kidneys, this pair of endocrine glands produces hormones including adrenaline, aldosterone, and cortisol. What organ is it?
Adrenal gland (also known as suprarenal glands) are endocrine glands that produce a variety of hormones including adrenaline and the steroids aldosterone and cortisol.
Its type species, a common freshwater organism constantly studied in classrooms and labs, lends its name to an entire genus of shape-changing single-celled organisms — what's the genus?
Amoeba (genus) is a genus of single-celled amoeboids in the family Amoebidae.
Marked by right lower abdominal pain, nausea, and fever, this common inflammatory condition is typically caused by a blockage from a small hard mass called a fecalith — name the condition?
Appendicitis is inflammation of the appendix.
Derived from a particular acid, this class of depressant drugs once treated anxiety and insomnia, but their overdose risk got them largely replaced by benzodiazepines and 'Z-drugs' — what are they?
Barbiturate are a class of depressant drugs that are chemically derived from barbituric acid.
Represented most commonly as a 1 or a 0, this portmanteau of 'binary digit' is the most fundamental unit of information in computing — what is it called?
Bit is the most basic unit of information in computing and digital communication.
Splitting from the windpipe at the carina into a right and left branch, this airway keeps forking into ever-smaller tubes until it's too narrow for cartilage support — what is it?
Bronchus (pl.: bronchi) is a passage or airway in the lower respiratory tract that conducts air into the lungs.
From starch that stores energy to the cellulose that stiffens plants and the chitin in insect shells, this biomolecule family is essentially sugars and their derivatives — what is it?
Carbohydrate is a sugar (saccharide) or a sugar derivative.

This perennial flowering herb is the only species of its onion-relative genus native to both the New World and Old World, prized for its edible leaves and flowers and also used to repel insects. What herb is this?
Chives is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaryllidaceae.

Produced by a mammal's mammary glands in the first days after birth, this antibody-rich milk helps protect newborns like calves and human infants from infection before regular milk takes over — which substance?
Colostrum (from Latin, of unknown origin), also known as foremilk, is the milk expressed by the mammary glands of a female mammal during the first few days following delivery of the newborn.
Mostly aquatic mandibulate arthropods, this group spans shrimp, crayfish, copepods, and barnacles — and modern science now files insects in alongside them — what are they?
Crustacean (from Latin word "crustacea" meaning: "those with shells" or "crusted ones") are mandibulate arthropods that are traditionally a part of the paraphyletic subphylum Crustacea.
Birds are the only surviving lineage of these warmblooded Mesozoic reptiles, having evolved from theropods in the Late Jurassic — what is the broader group called?
Dinosaur are a diverse group of warmblooded reptiles of the clade Dinosauria.
This is the only surviving member of its order, the Proboscidea, and its tusks are actually overgrown incisor teeth used as both weapons and tools — what animal is it?
Elephant are the largest living land animals.
This ground-nesting songbird of Europe and the Palearctic sings its signature tune while hovering high over farmland and heath, and now also breeds in Australia and Hawaii — what is it?
Eurasian skylark (Alauda arvensis), commonly referred to in Europe as the lark, is a passerine bird in the lark family, Alaudidae.
This genus in the rose family includes more than 20 species prized for their sweet-to-tart edible fruits, with domestic hybrids grown worldwide — what is its scientific name?
Fragaria is a genus of flowering plants in the rose family, Rosaceae, commonly known as strawberries for their edible fruits.
Before he founded a piece of the U.S. aircraft industry, this pioneer set an unofficial world speed record astride a V8-powered motorcycle that stood unbroken until 1911. Who was he?
Glenn Curtiss (May 21, 1878 - July 23, 1930) was an American aviation and motorcycling pioneer, and a founder of the U.S.
Caused by a group of enteroviruses, this common infection opens with a fever and then sprinkles blistering spots on exactly the three body parts named in its label. What is it?
Hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) is a common infection caused by a group of enteroviruses. It typically begins with a fever and feeling generally unwell.
This small rodent, with a pointed snout and a long, nearly hairless tail, has thrived by living alongside humans to the point that truly wild populations are now rare — what animal is it?
House mouse (Mus musculus) is a small mammal of the rodent family Muridae, characteristically having a pointed snout, large rounded ears, and a long and almost hairless tail.
This post-transition metal, chemically similar to gallium and thallium, was identified spectroscopically in 1863 and takes its name from the indigo line in its spectrum — what element is it?
Indium is a chemical element; its symbol is In and its atomic number is 49.
Known as the sunroot or earth apple, this central-North-American member of the sunflower family is cultivated for its tuber rather than its bloom — what is it?
Jerusalem artichoke (Helianthus tuberosus), also called sunroot, sunchoke, wild sunflower, topinambur, or earth apple, is a species of sunflower native to central North America.
This American biologist and one-time Communist Party member had four husbands, the last being the physicist who led Los Alamos — who was she?
Kitty Oppenheimer (ne Puening; August 8, 1910 - October 27, 1972) was an American biologist, botanist, and a member of the Communist Party of America until leaving in the 1930s.
Viruses muddy its definition, and it might exist beyond Earth in unfamiliar forms — but on this planet it fills air, water and soil, even harsh niches of extremophiles. What is it?
Life is the capacity, in matter, for processes such as cell signaling, homeostasis, metabolism, cell growth, adaptation, response to stimuli, and reproduction.
This alpha-amino acid, a building block for many proteins, carries a side chain that stays partially charged at the body's normal pH, classifying it among the basic amino acids — what is it?
Lysine (symbol Lys or K) is an -amino acid that is a precursor to many proteins.

These aquatic insects carry ancient traits from the first flying insects — long tails and wings that won't fold flat — and their water-dwelling young are a living signal of clean, unpolluted streams; what bug is this?
Mayfly (also up-winged flies or up-wing flies, or drake-flies in the UK; shadflies or fishflies in northern U.S.

This synthetic prostaglandin drug can prevent stomach ulcers in people taking NSAIDs, induce labor, treat dangerous postpartum bleeding, and — alone or paired with another drug — end a pregnancy — what's the medication?

Misoprostol is a synthetic prostaglandin medication used to prevent and treat stomach and duodenal ulcers, induce labor, cause an abortion, and treat postpartum bleeding due to poor contraction of the uterus.
This leafy Brassica rapa crop, native to the area around Beijing, became a widespread vegetable across Europe, the Americas, and Australia in the 1900s — which vegetable?
Napa cabbage (Brassica rapa subsp. In much of the world, it is referred to as "Chinese cabbage".
This condition causes involuntary, repetitive eye movements, sometimes present from birth and sometimes acquired later in life, often reducing visual clarity. Name the condition?
Nystagmus is a condition of involuntary (or voluntary, in some cases) eye movement.
This Felidae subfamily, first described in 1917 as covering only the big cats, later expanded to include the clouded leopard genus as well — which subfamily?

Pantherinae is a subfamily of the Felidae; it was named and first described by Reginald Innes Pocock in 1917 as only including the Panthera species, but later also came to include the clouded leopards (genus Neofelis).
Its Nahuatl-derived name means 'caterpillar cocoon,' and this small, spineless desert cactus native to northern Mexico and south Texas contains the psychoactive alkaloid mescaline — what's the plant?
Peyote is a small, spineless cactus which contains psychoactive alkaloids, particularly mescaline.

This genus of fragrant flowering shrubs, native to Mexico, Central America, and the Caribbean, is widely grown as an ornamental in Hawaii and in desert climates of the Arabian Peninsula — name the genus?
Plumeria is a genus of flowering plants in the family Apocynaceae.
This Eurasian fruit tree, also called the cherry plum, is believed to be one of the ancestral parents of the plum we cultivate today — what species is it?
Prunus cerasifera is a species of plum known by the common names cherry plum and myrobalan plum.
This biological process by which new organisms are produced from parents comes in two forms — one requiring a single organism, the other requiring two. What is it?
Reproduction (or procreation or breeding) is the biological process by which new individual organisms - offspring - are produced from their parent or parents.

Originally conceived in the 1960s as a jet trainer before evolving into a supersonic strike aircraft, this joint British-French warplane — retired by both original operators — remains in service only with the Indian Air Force. Name it?
SEPECAT Jaguar is a British-French supersonic jet attack aircraft originally used by the British Royal Air Force and the French Air Force in the close air support and nuclear strike role.

Triggered by certain serotonergic medications, this group of symptoms can range from mild high blood pressure to severe, potentially fatal spikes in body temperature and dangerous muscle breakdown — what's it called?
Serotonin syndrome (SS) consists of a group of symptoms that may occur with the use of certain serotonergic medications or drugs.
Native to a swath from Ireland to southern China, this aromatic herb is used to flavor food and herbal teas, and its extracted oil serves as both a flavoring and a scent — what is it?

Spearmint (Mentha spicata), also known as garden mint, common mint, lamb mint and mackerel mint, is native to Europe and southern temperate Asia, extending from Ireland in the west to southern China in the east.
This Chinese physician and revolutionary led the 1911 Revolution, overthrew the Qing dynasty, and founded the Republic of China as its first president. Who was he?
Sun Yat-sen (12 November 1866 - 12 March 1925) was a Chinese physician, revolutionary and political philosopher who founded the Republic of China (ROC) and the Kuomintang (KMT).
What common name covers a group of spike-leaved flowering plants — mostly in the daisy family — whose prickles evolved purely to ward off hungry herbivores?
Thistle is the common name of a group of flowering plants characterised by leaves with sharp spikes on the margins, mostly in the family Asteraceae.
Native to Central and South America but now found in sub-Saharan Africa, which parasitic flea burrows into skin to cause the condition tungiasis?
Tunga penetrans is a species of flea also known as the jigger, jigger flea, chigoe, chigo, chigoe flea, chigo flea, nigua, sand flea, or burrowing flea.

Manufactured under license by both Goodyear and Brewster during World War II, this American carrier-based fighter aircraft became one of the most capable fighter-bombers of the war and later saw service in Korea — which aircraft?
Vought F4U Corsair is an American fighter aircraft that saw service primarily in World War II and the Korean War.
Also called humped cattle for the fatty growth on its shoulders, this South Asian breed group is used for everything from plowing to dairy, and even kept as pets in miniature form — what is it?
Zebu (Bos indicus), also known as indicine cattle and humped cattle, is a species or subspecies of domestic cattle originating in South Asia.
Located behind the nasal cavity where the nose meets the throat, which mass of lymphoid tissue is also known as the pharyngeal tonsil?
Adenoid: Type of tonsil. The adenoid, also known as the pharyngeal tonsil, or nasopharyngeal tonsil is the superior-most of the tonsils.

Born out of wedlock in the Caribbean and orphaned young, this Founding Father became the first U.S. secretary of the treasury and started America's first political party, the Federalist Party — who was he?

Capable of constantly changing its shape by extending and retracting temporary 'false feet,' this single-celled organism turns up across nearly every branch of the eukaryotic tree of life — what is it?
Central to the 18th-century chemical revolution, this French nobleman named oxygen in 1778 and overturned the phlogiston theory of combustion — who is he?
Antoine Lavoisier: French nobleman and chemist (1743–1794)
This order of even-toed hoofed mammals turns out to include whales and dolphins, molecular biology having revealed their close kinship to hippos — what order is it?
Artiodactyla: Order of mammals. Artiodactyla ( AR-tee-oh-DAK-tih-lə; from Ancient Greek ἄρτιος ártios 'even' and δάκτυλος dáktylos 'finger, toe') is an order of placental mammals.
Sold under the brand name Lioresal, this muscle relaxant treats spasticity from spinal cord injuries or MS and is sometimes used off-label for alcohol withdrawal — what is it?
Baclofen: Gabapentinoid and Skeletal Muscle Relaxant.
Native to Southeast Asia, the heart-shaped leaves of this pepper-family vine are chewed with areca nut, despite links to serious health risks — which plant?
Betel: Species of plant. Betel (Piper betle) is a species of flowering plant in the pepper family Piperaceae, native to Southeast Asia.
Launched as the 7X7 program in 1978 and designed to complement the larger 747, which American wide-body airliner first entered service with United Airlines in 1982?
This Asian insect species, first found in Pennsylvania in 1998, cost Mid-Atlantic apple growers $37 million in a single year and now threatens hazelnut harvests worldwide — what is it?

Brown marmorated stink bug: Species of Pentatomid insect. The brown marmorated stink bug (Halyomorpha halys) is an insect in the family Pentatomidae, native to China, Japan, Korea, and other Asian regions.
Cultivated since China's Song Dynasty and boasting thousands of ornamental cultivars, which flowering shrub from the tea family is native to forests of China and Japan?
Camellia japonica: Species of flowering plant.
Nicknamed the pudding-pipe tree, this Fabaceae-family plant is the national tree of Thailand and doubles as the state flower of Kerala and Delhi — which species?

Cassia fistula: Species of flowering plant. Cassia fistula, also known as golden shower, purging cassia, Indian laburnum, kani konna, or pudding-pipe tree, is a flowering plant in the family Fabaceae.
Capable of sprinting up to 104 km/h, this spotted big cat is the fastest land animal alive, sporting black tear-like streaks down its face and a flexible spine built for speed — which animal?
Cheetah: Large feline of the genus Acinonyx.
Dubbed the 'father of information theory,' this polymath was the first to apply Boolean algebra to digital circuits and helped found the field of artificial intelligence — who is he?
Blue above and orange below, this sparrow-sized bird dives for fish and nests in burrows dug into riverbanks — which species?
Common kingfisher: Species of bird. It is resident in much of its range, but migrates from areas where rivers freeze in winter.
Also known as hawthorn, quickthorn, or May-tree, this genus of several hundred shrub and tree species in the rose family is native across the temperate Northern Hemisphere — which genus?
Crataegus: Genus of flowering plants in the rose family Rosaceae.

Developed as a successor to an earlier delta-wing fighter family, this French all-weather interceptor entered service with the French Air Force in 1974, equipped with Cyrano IV radar — what aircraft is it?
Dassault Mirage F1: French attack aircraft. During the 1960s, Dassault commenced development of what would become the Mirage F1 as a private venture, alongside the larger Mirage F2.
Native to North Africa and West Asia, this annual herb in the celery family lends its leaves and seeds as both an herb and a spice — what is it?
Dill: Species of flowering plant in the celery family Apiaceae.

This medical term covers abnormal cell or organ growth — from hip conditions to bone marrow disorders — and is generally distinguished from cancerous neoplasia, though some forms are precancerous. What is it called?
Dysplasia: Abnormal development, at macroscopic or microscopical level.
Australia's tallest native bird, this flightless species can sprint up to 48 kilometers per hour and often goes weeks without drinking water — which bird?
Emu: Large flightless bird endemic to Australia.
Every animal, plant, fungus and seaweed belongs to this domain, defined by one shared cellular feature: a nucleus wrapped in its own membrane. What are they called?
Eukaryote: Domain of life whose cells have nuclei.
Its 41 living species boast the most varied fur patterns of any land carnivore, all armed with retractile claws and an obligate taste for meat — which family is this?
Felidae: Family of mammals. Felidae ( FEE-lə-dee) is the family of mammals in the order Carnivora colloquially referred to as cats.
This infection and inflammation of hair follicles produces pimples with white tips anywhere on hair-covered skin — what is the condition called?
Folliculitis: Human and animal disease of follicles.
Native to Central Asia and a close relative of the onion, shallot, and leek, this bulbous Allium has been a seasoning and folk remedy known to Babylonians, Egyptians, and Romans alike — what is it?
This American chemist helped synthesize ten transuranium elements, dreamed up the actinide concept, and advised ten US presidents on nuclear policy — who shared the 1951 Nobel for that work?
Marketed under the brand name Mucinex, this expectorant medication has been used to loosen chest congestion since at least 1933 — what is it?
Guaifenesin: Expectorant medication. It may be used in combination with other medications.

Formally described only in 1983, this helical, flagella-driven bacterium burrows through the stomach's mucous lining and is the chief culprit behind gastric ulcers and some stomach cancers. What is it?
Nicknamed 'Hobbit,' this extinct species of small archaic humans stood about 1.1 meters tall and lived on the Indonesian island of Flores until roughly 50,000 years ago — which species?
Homo floresiensis: Extinct small human species found in Flores.

Typically begun with an induction of preliminary instructions, this state of focused attention and heightened suggestibility is debated as either an altered trance or a form of imaginative role-play — what is it?
Hypnosis: State of increased suggestibility. There are competing theories explaining hypnosis and related phenomena.
The global network of networks links private, public, academic, business and government networks using which protocol suite?
The Internet is the global system of interconnected computer networks that uses the Internet protocol suite (TCP/IP) to communicate between networks and devices.
He won the Fields Medal in 1954 and, nearly half a century later, the very first Abel Prize in 2003 — which French mathematician of algebraic topology and geometry is it?

Conceived as a high-speed 'Schnellbomber' for the German Luftwaffe, this twin-engined WWII aircraft evolved into everything from a night fighter to the explosive lower half of composite 'Mistel' combinations — what is it?
Junkers Ju 88: German twin-engined multirole combat aircraft.
Situated between two larger folds of skin, these paired flaps extend from the inner vaginal and urethral openings and form the clitoral hood above — which structures are these?
Labia minora: Flaps of skin on either side of the vaginal opening in the vulva.

This French chemist's discoveries in fermentation and vaccination gave us a heat-treatment process that now bears his name and rabies and anthrax vaccines — who was he?
Louis Pasteur: French chemist, pharmacist and microbiologist (1822–1895)
Distinguished from living elephants by spirally twisted tusks and a thick coat of fur for cold climates, this extinct genus survived from the late Miocene until roughly 4,000 years ago — what was it?
Mammoth: Extinct genus of mammals. The oldest mammoth representative, Mammuthus subplanifrons, appeared around 6 million years ago during the late Miocene in southern and Eastern Africa.

Marked by small white Koplik spots inside the mouth and a red rash that starts on the face before spreading, this highly contagious, vaccine-preventable disease can bring fevers over 40°C — which disease?
Son of a U.S. vice president, this young art collector vanished in 1961 during an expedition into New Guinea's Asmat region, with some accounts claiming he was killed by local tribesmen — who was he?
Michael Rockefeller: American anthropologist and art collector (1938–1961)
Named in 1883 by a German anthropologist who wrongly believed it was most common among his patients, this bluish congenital birthmark usually fades by puberty — what is it?
Mongolian spot: Type of birthmark. It normally disappears three to five years after birth and almost always by puberty.
Most often triggered by a viral infection and capable of progressing to heart failure or cardiac arrest, which condition involves inflammation of the heart muscle itself?

Myocarditis: Inflammation of the heart muscle. Myocarditis can progress to inflammatory cardiomyopathy when there is associated ventricular remodeling and cardiac dysfunction due to chronic inflammation.
An oily alkaloid from nightshade plants like tobacco, it doubles as a potent insect neurotoxin and once served as an insecticide, inspiring the neonicotinoid pesticides — what is it?
Nicotine: Chemical stimulant produced by some plants.
This physics principle states that current through a conductor is directly proportional to the voltage across it, expressed as V equals I times R — what's it called?
Ohm's law: Law of electrical current and voltage. Ohm's law states that the electric current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
A reactive nonmetal of the chalcogen group, it's the most abundant element in Earth's crust — locked into water, silicates, and rust — and the third-most abundant in the universe. What is it?
Oxygen: Chemical element with atomic number 8 (O)
This hickory species native to the Mississippi River region produces a nut used in praline candy and a famous holiday pie, and is the official state tree of Texas — what is it?
Pecan: Species of nut tree native to the southern USA and northern Mexico.
This branch of linguistics studies how speech sounds are articulated, transmitted as sound waves, and perceived, split into three sub-disciplines — what field is it?
Phonetics: Study of how humans produce and perceive sounds.
Sometimes called a 'collapsed lung,' this condition involves air trapped in the space between the lung and chest wall, causing sudden sharp one-sided chest pain — what is it?
Pneumothorax: Abnormal collection of air in the pleural space.
Manufactured in a soybean-oil emulsion that gives it a milky white look, this IV anesthetic — sold as Diprivan — induces unconsciousness fast and lets patients wake quickly; what is it?
Propofol: Intravenous medication used in anesthesia.
Guided by empiricist and positivist philosophy, which academic methodology turns data collection into numbers to test theories across the natural, applied, formal, and social sciences?
Quantitative research: All procedures for the numerical representation of empirical facts.
Native to South and Southeast Asia, this non-venomous constrictor is the world's longest snake and has been spotted swimming far out at sea — what species is it?
Reticulated python: Species of snake. It is the world's longest snake, and the third heaviest after the green anaconda and Burmese python.

Sold under the brand name Crestor, this medication lowers cholesterol by inhibiting an enzyme in the liver called HMG-CoA reductase, and was the twelfth most commonly prescribed drug in the US in 2023. What is it?
Rosuvastatin: Statin medication. It is recommended to be used with dietary changes, exercise, and weight loss.
Also called a green onion, this mild Allium vegetable has a slender green stem but never develops a bulb like its garlic and leek relatives — what is it?
Scallion: Edible vegetable of various species in the genus Allium.
Nicknamed the 'Human Computer' for her lightning mental arithmetic, this Indian writer also authored one of the earliest studies of homosexuality in India, back in 1977 — who is she?
Shakuntala Devi: Indian writer and mental calculator (1929–2013)

Historically mined in vast deposits and nicknamed 'Chile saltpeter,' this white, water-soluble alkali metal compound is used in fertilizers, fireworks, meat preservation, and solid rocket fuel. What is it?
Sodium nitrate: Chemical compound. The mineral form is also known as nitratine, nitratite or soda niter.
This physics law states that a black body's radiated energy per unit area is proportional to the fourth power of its absolute temperature — which law?
Stefan–Boltzmann law: Physical law on the emissive power of black body.
Time named this marine biologist its first "Hero for the Planet" in 1998, the same year she became a National Geographic Explorer — and she'd already been NOAA's first chief scientist. Who is she?
Sylvia Earle: American marine biologist and lecturer.
Developed under the codename 'WhiteStar' and unveiled in Hawthorne, California in 2009, this full-size electric sedan won Motor Trend's Car of the Year in 2013 — which car?
Tesla Model S: Battery-electric full-size car. The Tesla Model S is a battery-electric, four-door full-size car that was produced by the American automaker Tesla from 2012 to 2026.
Commonly called jock itch, this contagious fungal infection of the groin and buttocks causes an intensely itchy, red, scaly rash with a well-defined curved border — what is it?
Tinea cruris: Fungal infection. It is often associated with athlete's foot and fungal nail infections, excessive sweating, and sharing of infected towels or sports clothing.

Found only in the northern Gulf of California, this porpoise is the smallest living cetacean and is critically endangered due to bycatch from an illegal fishery — which species?
Vaquita: Endangered species of porpoise. The vaquita ( və-KEE-tə; Phocoena sinus) is a species of porpoise endemic to the northern end of the Gulf of California in Baja California, Mexico.

This German American aerospace engineer and space architect (1912–1977) initially worked in Nazi Germany's rocket development program and later led rocket and space technology development in the US — who is he?
Wernher von Braun: German American aerospace engineer (1912–1977). The V-2 became the first artificial object to travel into space by crossing the Kármán line on 20 June 1944.
This citrus fruit of Chinese origin is believed to be a natural hybrid of a wild mandarin subspecies and the ichang papeda — what fruit?
Yuzu: Citrus fruit and plant. Yuzu (Citrus × junos, from Japanese 柚子 or ユズ;) is a citrus fruit and plant in the family Rutaceae of Chinese origin.
